docs.task: How review findings are split and sent to the fix agent, including the resolve-review judge and the auto-fixable path.

asks: Explain how review findings are split.
Explain how findings are sent to the fix agent.

data_flow.step: The planner spawns `code-reviewer` for the loop (LoopNext::Review). The runner records the project's auto-fixable rule IDs in the execution's `params` under `auto_fixable_ids`, excluding IDs starting `SEC-BLOCK` or `PHASE-REQ`.
The reviewer submits `CodeReviewerSubmit { findings, security_block, ledger_path, summary }`. ExecutionFinished is folded; `on_finished` calls `loop_finished` for any execution with a loop key.
Errors, interruptions and a missing submit are handled first (retry once, rerun, or LoopNext::Failed). For a readable review: `iterations += 1`, `last_review` is stored.

BLOCKER branch: if `security_block` or any finding has severity Blocker, `blocker_open = true` and the next step is a `BlockerFix` work pass whose instructions are only the BLOCKER findings plus a removal instruction. No cap, nothing else is sent (HIGH, MEDIUM, and auto-fixable findings in the same pass are dropped and re-found by the next review).
Otherwise each finding is classified by `auto_fixable()` into `apply`, HIGH or MEDIUM `remaining`, or LOW `low` (stored as `leftover_low`).

Auto-fixable path: when `apply` is non-empty, `LoopNext::Autofix { apply, remaining }`. The planner emits `Step::Autofix`, and the runner calls `autofix::apply_findings(project_root, findings)` on a blocking thread, then appends `SessionEvent::AutofixApplied { applied, failed }`. No agent runs and the ledger is not written.

The fold of AutofixApplied: for each failed (rule_line, reason) it finds the matching `apply` finding by `f.line()`; only those with severity High or Medium are appended to `remaining` (a failed LOW auto-fixable finding is dropped silently, and the failure reason is not passed on). It then calls `after_findings(rem, ...)`.

`after_findings`: empty remaining means Stage (or Done when staging is off), with no re-review of the engine's own edits. Iterations at or above `effective_cap` (3, or 10 under YOLO, plus `extra_cap`) means CapReached (non-YOLO) or Resolve (YOLO). Otherwise `LoopNext::Work { kind: Fix, instructions: fix_instructions(remaining, ledger) }`.

Planner `loop_work` picks the agent: `work_agent` for Initial (and a first Rerun/Resume), otherwise `fix_agent` (Implementer for the build loop, WriteTest for the test loop). It sets `SpawnInputs.work`, `instructions`, and `ledger_file` for Fix and BlockerFix. `factory::work_extras` maps `instructions` into the spawn's findings text. Per CLAUDE.md and the pipeline docs a fix continues the last worker's conversation when the agent is the same (Rule H5).

The fix agent edits code and writes FIXED or WONTFIX lines with rationale into the review ledger, then submits an ImplementerSubmit. On `SubmitStatus::Ok` the loop goes to `LoopNext::Review` again, and `l.rationale` keeps the fix instructions for the next reviewer spawn.

Cap and Resolve path: at the cap a non-YOLO session opens a `ReviewCap` gate with the open findings; `another-pass` bumps `extra_cap` and sends the same fix_instructions (plus optional user text, routed through the Route answer judge when routed); any other answer blocks the phase. Under YOLO the planner asks the Resolve-review judge (`Step::Judge`, subject `phase:N` or `phase:N-tests` via loop_key_str). The judge input is the open findings, review ledger excerpt, phase file excerpt and counts. `fix` leads to one fix pass with the judge's per-finding instructions and one extra verification review; after that review, `after_findings` re-enters Resolve only while open count is below `open_before_resolve` (converging), else Blocked.

patterns.description: When a Review execution finishes, SessionState::loop_finished (in the pure fold) reads the project's auto-fixable rule IDs from the execution's recorded params, computes a per-finding auto flag, then partitions: BLOCKER (or security_block) short-circuits to a BlockerFix; otherwise each finding goes to `apply` (auto), `remaining` (HIGH or MEDIUM, not auto), or `low` (everything else). LOW non-auto findings are stored in `leftover_low` for the completion report. If `apply` is non-empty the loop goes to LoopNext::Autofix { apply, remaining }; otherwise WorkLoop::after_findings(remaining, ...) decides: empty remaining means Stage or Done; iterations at the cap means CapReached (or Resolve under YOLO); otherwise LoopNext::Work { kind: Fix, instructions: fix_instructions(...) }.
patterns.name: Fold-time split of findings, using a fact recorded in the spawn event

patterns.description: A finding is auto-fixable only when it is not BLOCKER, its rule does not start with SEC-BLOCK or PHASE-REQ, and its rule ID is in the project's list. The same exclusions are applied a second time when the list is built (ProjectProfile::auto_fixable_ids). Severity is not otherwise considered, so an auto-fixable HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW finding is all applied by the engine.
patterns.name: Auto-fixable predicate

patterns.description: The runner, at spawn of a Review execution, inserts the profile's auto-fixable IDs into the ExecutionStarted params so the fold does not have to read project.toml.
patterns.name: Auto-fixable IDs recorded in params at spawn (pattern 1 in CLAUDE.md)

patterns.description: HIGH and MEDIUM findings go verbatim (ReviewFinding::line()) in one block, with the ledger path and an instruction to record FIXED or WONTFIX with rationale per finding. BLOCKER text is different: only BLOCKER findings, with an instruction to remove the code, not rewrite it. The planner passes the string as SpawnInputs.instructions with the ledger path; factory::work_extras maps it to the spawn's findings field.
patterns.name: Fix text sent to the fix agent

patterns.description: A decision event for JudgeKind::ResolveReview is applied in SessionState::on_decision, only while the loop is in LoopNext::Resolve. `fix` increments resolve_rounds, records open_before_resolve, raises extra_cap by 1 (one verification review), and sets LoopNext::Work { Fix } whose text is the judge's per-finding instructions (or fix_instructions of the open findings when the judge returned no instructions). `block` sets LoopNext::Blocked with the judge's reason and the ledger path. The decision cannot be overridden (can_override returns false for it).
patterns.name: Resolve-review judge applied in the fold

document.problem: After a code-reviewer pass, the engine partitions the findings by severity, rule and the project's auto-fixable rule IDs, applies some mechanically, sends HIGH and MEDIUM to a fix agent verbatim, and keeps LOW ones for the report. Only at the review budget under YOLO does a model (the Resolve-review judge) look at the open findings. No step between the reviewer's submit and the fix agent evaluates whether a finding is correct, so a false-positive HIGH or MEDIUM finding always reaches the fix agent.
document.scope: Task: how review findings are split and sent to the fix agent, including the resolve-review judge and the auto-fixable path. Covers the engine fold, planner, runner, autofix applier, judge, prompts, tests, and docs for the implement and test review loops. It does not cover the web UI rendering of findings, the Rescue/Route-answer judges beyond where they touch the fix text, or any proposed new judge.
document.title: Review findings split, fix-agent routing, resolve-review judge, and the auto-fixable path

submit.findings_summary: The split happens in the pure fold, `SessionState::loop_finished` in state.rs. BLOCKER findings go alone to a BlockerFix pass. The rest are split into auto-fixable (rule ID recorded in the review's params, excluding SEC-BLOCK and PHASE-REQ), HIGH/MEDIUM (sent verbatim to the fix agent via `fix_instructions`, with the ledger path), and LOW (kept as `leftover_low`). Auto-fixable findings are applied by `autofix::apply_findings` through `Step::Autofix`, with no agent run. Failed HIGH/MEDIUM ones rejoin the fix list, but a failed LOW one is dropped. If nothing remains after the autofix, the loop stages without re-review. At the cap, a non-YOLO session gets a ReviewCap gate. Under YOLO the Resolve-review judge returns `fix` (per-finding instructions plus one verification review) or `block`, and it repeats only while the open count falls. Nothing before the fix agent checks whether a finding is a false positive. Conformance fixtures, prompts, and docs that cover this are listed in the document.

data_flow.step: The planner finds a missing fact and returns `Step::Judge { judge, subject }` from `next_steps(&SessionState, &PlanCtx)`.
The runner dispatches the step by `Step::Judge { judge, subject } => self.perform_judge(session, judge, subject)`.

perform_judge takes a state snapshot, builds `(input, summary)` with `judge_input::judge_input(&st, kind, subject, &self.project_facts())` and the schema with `output_schema(kind, None)`, and defines the per-kind `validate` closure.

call_judge loads the system prompt with `factory.judge_prompt(kind.as_str())` (error 'No prompt for the <kind> judge.' when missing) and resolves the `judge` route at `Tier::Advanced` via `resolve_route`.

`Services::judge(route, system, input, schema, Effort::Low)` runs one forced `decide` tool call through `ostra_providers::structured`; usage cost is added to `judge_cost` for the session. Up to 3 attempts; a result that fails `validate` or a provider error is retried.

On a valid value, `append(SessionEvent::DecisionMade { id: DecisionId::new(), judge, subject, input_summary, output, reason: reason_of(&value) })`. Inner::append stores, folds, broadcasts, and wakes the driver.

The fold records the decision and calls `on_decision(..., overriding = false)`, which deserializes `output` into the Out struct and updates session state (for example `self.stakes = Some((id, out.stakes))`, `self.set_track(out.track)`, `self.completion_decision = Some(id)`).
On the next `next_steps` call the planner sees the new state and no longer pushes the judge, and proceeds to the next rule.

Override path: POST /api/decisions/{id}/override calls `Engine::override_decision`, which checks `can_override`, validates the new output against the Out struct for the kinds listed, writes `mark_overridden` to the db, and appends `DecisionOverridden`; the fold calls `on_decision(..., overriding = true)`.

patterns.description: A judge's shape exists three times and nothing ties them together except tests: (1) the serde struct in judge.rs with `#[serde(default)] reason: String` (every output carries `reason`, read by reason_of); (2) an arm in `output_schema` with `required` listing every field the model must send; (3) an arm in the `validate` closure in `perform_judge` that does `serde_json::from_value::<XOut>(v.clone()).is_ok()` (Feedback additionally requires non-empty targets; YoloAnswer returns true). A value failing validate is retried up to 3 attempts total with 500 ms times attempt back-off, then the session fails (Completion falls back to a state-only report; YoloAnswer leaves the gate open with a Note). Fields the fold treats as optional are `#[serde(default)]` in the struct but still listed in `required` in the schema (see Stakes, Track).

patterns.description: `judge_input` is a single `match kind` with no wildcard arm, so a new JudgeKind fails to compile until an arm is added. Each arm writes Markdown sections with `writeln!` into one String (`# Request`, facts about the session, excerpts of files on disk via `excerpt`/`excerpt_n`) and returns a short summary stored on the decision as input_summary. The subject string carries the thing the judge is about (a gate id, an execution id, 'phase,tests' loop key via parse_loop_key, a comma list of explore task indexes, an amendment index, a feedback round index). The prompt describes the same sections in its `## Input` paragraph.

patterns.description: `assets/judges/<as_str>.md`. Structure used by stakes.md and resolve-review.md: H1 '<Name> judge', one paragraph on the situation and why, `## Input` (what the user message holds), `## Decide` (table or bullets of the choices, then the lean direction with a 'because' clause), `## Output` ('Call `decide` once with <fields> and `reason`: one or two sentences for the user'). The prompt must name `decide`, which the test judges_and_references_resolve asserts. Rule IDs are cited in the prompt when the judge implements a rule. snippet.code:
## Output

Call `decide` once with `stakes` (`low`, `medium`, or `high`) and `reason`: one or two sentences for the user
naming the spec facts that decided it.

patterns.description: The planner pushes `Step::Judge { judge, subject }` when a fact the next step needs is missing from fold state, and stops pushing once the fold has recorded it. The guard is fold state, not the event log: Classify checks `s.classify.is_none()`, Track checks `s.track` is `None`, Stakes checks `s.stakes` is `None`, Completion checks `s.completion_decision`, Sufficiency checks per-task `judged` flags and `sufficiency_rounds < SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS`, Rescue/ResolveReview/RouteAnswer are keyed by the loop's `LoopNext` variant (`Rescue`, `Resolve`/`CapReached` under YOLO, `AwaitRoute`). Step::key() is 'judge:<kebab>:<subject>' so the runner does not start the same judge twice while one is in flight. The step carries no input; the runner builds it from a state snapshot. A new rule needs a fixture in tests/conformance/main.rs (Rule citation in a one-line comment).
patterns.name: Planner step: a pure rule that pushes Step::Judge until fold state records the decision

patterns.description: `SessionEvent::DecisionMade` inserts a decision record (overridden: false) and calls `on_decision(id, judge, subject, output, false)`. `on_decision` is an exhaustive `match judge`. Each arm deserializes the stored `output` into the `XOut` struct and applies it; an output that does not parse is ignored (Stakes, Track, Rescue, ResolveReview, RouteAnswer, Feedback) except Classify, which sets `failed`. Arms also check that the decision is still relevant (Rescue requires `LoopNext::Rescue` for the same exec; ResolveReview requires `LoopNext::Resolve`; Feedback requires round route to be `None`) so a stale decision is dropped. The fold must stay a pure function of the log: any outside fact must be recorded in the event.
patterns.name: Fold: on_decision matches on JudgeKind and tolerates bad output

patterns.description: An override is allowed only for Classify, Stakes, Track, and Sufficiency; every other kind returns `false` from the `_ =>` arm of `SessionState::can_override`. Overriding needs edits in these places: (1) `can_override` arm (the `_ => false` arm is a wildcard so a new kind is silently non-overridable); (2) the `valid` match in `Engine::override_decision` in runner.rs, whose `_ => false` arm makes the API return 'The override does not match the decision's output shape.' for any kind not listed; (3) the `overriding` branch of the kind's arm in `on_decision`, which re-checks the same condition because a late override event may arrive (Classify uses can_override_classify_now, Stakes and Track re-check, Sufficiency removes unstarted Sufficiency-origin explore tasks). `DecisionView.can_override` is computed from `can_override`, so the UI button needs no change. The `decisions` table also has a `can_override` column with `set_can_override` in ostra-store; the view value comes from the fold.
patterns.name: Override: three gates must all agree

document.problem: A judge is a single forced-schema model call whose result is stored as a DecisionMade event and applied by the fold. Adding one touches a closed enum in ostra-core, three files in ostra-engine (judge.rs, judge_input.rs, plan.rs/state.rs/runner.rs), one embedded prompt asset, tests, evals, docs and a TypeScript switch. Several of these places are exhaustive matches that fail to compile for a new variant, and several are not (override, validation of overrides, docs tables, evals), so the full list has to be known.
document.scope: Task: how a judge is added: its output struct and schema, input builder, prompt asset, the planner step, the fold, and overrides. Covers the existing code path for the ten JudgeKind variants and every place a new variant must be handled. It does not design any specific new judge and did not open the provider-level structured() implementation or the web UI beyond the exhaustive switch.
document.title: Adding a judge

submit.findings_summary: A judge is a JudgeKind variant (ostra-core event.rs) with an Out struct and a hand-written output_schema arm (judge.rs), a judge_input arm (judge_input.rs, an exhaustive match returning the user message and input_summary), and a prompt at assets/judges/<kebab-name>.md that must name `decide` (found by file stem, no registry). The planner pushes Step::Judge until fold state records the decision. The runner's perform_judge builds the input, schema and a validate closure, and call_judge retries 3 times and appends DecisionMade. The fold's on_decision (exhaustive match) applies the decision. Overrides are opt-in in three non-compiler-enforced places: can_override, the `valid` match in Engine::override_decision, and the `overriding` branch of on_decision. Other places to touch: a conformance fixture, the web events.ts switch, the regenerated JudgeKind.ts, the hand-listed prompt test, the e2e scripted judge, the evals, and docs/internals/gates-and-judges.md.

tests/evals/judges.toml case format and judge_evals.rs scoring
